blocks.description: Tests whether variants differ from the control on conversion rate (z-test) or mean (Welch's t-test), with lift, confidence intervals, p-values, verdicts and required sample size.
Classifies items into A, B and C by cumulative share of value (Pareto), optionally within groups, plus XYZ demand-variability classes for ABC-XYZ inventory analysis.
Measures how often every pair of items is bought together (support, confidence, lift, Jaccard) from basket data, with each item's strongest partners.
Tests whether amounts follow Benford's law (first, first-two or second digit), overall or per group, with chi-square, MAD conformity and flagged records for follow-up.
From an event log: case durations and rework, the slowest and costliest handovers between activities, and activity statistics.
Kaplan-Meier retention curves with censoring, confidence bands, median lifetime, milestone retention and log-rank tests between groups.

Groups records into clusters by density (DBSCAN) on numeric fields and marks isolated records as noise. Outputs the input records with a Cluster field added: 1, 2, 3 and so on for clusters, 0 for noise.

Clusters records with a Gaussian mixture model on numeric fields, choosing the number of clusters itself, and gives each record its cluster and the probability that it belongs there. A second input can be assigned to the same clusters.
Groups records into a chosen number of clusters with k-means on numeric fields, standardised first. Outputs the input records with a Cluster field added.
Builds acquisition cohorts from activity or order data and measures retention and revenue per cohort over time, with an average retention curve.
HHI, Gini, top-N and top-20% shares and Lorenz curves for customer, supplier or market concentration, per group.
Cross-tabulates two categorical fields with shares, expected counts and residuals, and tests their association with chi-square and Cramer's V.
Pearson and Spearman correlations with p-values for all pairs of numeric fields or against a target, per group, ranked, with a heat-map matrix.
Apportions cost pools to departments, products or customers by drivers, with penny-exact largest-remainder rounding and a list of unallocated pools.
Historical and predictive customer lifetime value from orders (BG/NBD and Gamma-Gamma), with probability active, discounting and a holdout check.
Profiles a dataset: one record per field with its type, missing and distinct counts, most common value and statistics, and the records with z-scores and anomaly flags for every numeric field.
Finds the k nearest points in a second input for each point in the first, by great-circle distance, with an optional distance limit and a catchment summary per destination.
Compares forecasts with actuals per item and model: MAE, RMSE, MAPE, sMAPE, WAPE, bias and tracking signal, with flags, best model per item and a model ranking.
Builds conversion funnels from event data: users reaching each ordered step within an optional time window, conversion, drop-off and time between steps, per segment.
Histograms with automatic bin widths shared across groups, and distribution statistics (percentiles, skewness, kurtosis) per group.
Exponential smoothing forecasts per series with automatic trend and seasonality selection, prediction intervals and a holdout accuracy check.
Restates money values in real terms of a base period using a price index table, per series, with the index used and cumulative inflation.
NPV, IRR / XIRR, MIRR, payback, discounted payback and profitability index per project from cash flows, with NPV profiles and multiple-IRR warnings.
Summarises Likert-scale survey questions: answer distributions, mean scores, top-2-box, net scores and neutral shares, per question and segment.
Solves linear and integer programmes given as data (variables with objective and bounds, constraints in long format) with the HiGHS solver: optimal plan, slack, binding constraints and shadow prices.
Generates payment schedules for loans and leases (repayment, equal principal, interest only, with balloon), monthly, quarterly or annually, with a summary per loan.
Simulates three-point estimates and risk events to give P10 / P50 / P80 / P90 totals, contingency, the probability of exceeding a budget, and the drivers of uncertainty.
Net Promoter Score per group and period from 0-10 answers, with margin of error, confidence interval, weights, significance vs the rest and vs the previous period.

From a list of connections (each record: a node, the node it connects to, and the first node's category), measures how much each category's connections lead to nodes it shares with each other category, such as which departments work on the same projects.

Places the nodes of a network on a 2-D (or 1-D or 3-D) map with t-SNE, so that nodes connected to the same other nodes end up close together and nodes with different connections far apart. Input: one record per connection.
Occupancy over time from start and end times: average and peak concurrency per bucket, utilisation against capacity and time over capacity, per group.
The most common event sequences per user or session, step-numbered transitions for Sankey charts, and next-step probabilities.
Builds the standard month / QTD / YTD / moving annual total comparison versus prior periods per group, with a fiscal year start of your choice, plus a monthly trend table.
Finds which polygon (territory, zone, area) each latitude / longitude point falls in, from GeoJSON or WKT shapes, and counts points per polygon.
Great-circle distance, bearing, direction and midpoint between two latitude / longitude pairs per row, with optional road distance and travel time estimates.
Predicts a category for each record from the k most similar records whose category is known (k-nearest neighbours), on numeric fields standardised first, with the share of neighbours that agree.
Predicts a category (such as Normal, Worn or Faulty) for new records from numeric fields, using a support vector machine trained on records whose category is known.
Estimates price elasticity of demand per product with a log-log regression (optional control drivers), with confidence intervals, revenue impact and demand curves.
Laspeyres, Paasche and Fisher price indices, value and volume indices from item prices and quantities per period, per group.
Decomposes revenue change between two periods into volume, mix, price, new and lost product effects that add up exactly, per item and optional group.
PCA on numeric fields: explained variance, loadings and correlations, automatic or fixed number of components, and scores per row.
Item-to-item recommendations from purchase history: top new products per customer with the reason, and similar products per product.
Scores customers on recency, frequency and monetary value from transactions and assigns named segments such as Champions, At Risk and Lost, with a segment summary.
Matches two ledgers one-to-one on amount, reference and date with tolerances, plus group matches, and lists the unmatched items on each side.
Linear or logistic regression with coefficients, standard errors, p-values, confidence intervals, odds ratios, VIF, fit statistics and scored rows.
Running balances per account from opening balances and dated transactions, with lowest balance, days below zero or a limit, and average daily balance.
Calculates safety stock, reorder points, order-up-to levels and EOQ per item from demand history and lead times for a target service level, with a reorder list.
Sample size and power for A/B tests on proportions or means and for survey margins of error, per scenario, with days needed and power curves.
Splits time series into trend, seasonal and residual components (additive or multiplicative) with seasonally adjusted values, seasonal indices and strength measures.
Projects stock day by day from on-hand, demand and open purchase orders to give run-out dates, shortfalls and what to expedite.

Estimates survival (or retention) curves from time-to-event data with censoring, by the Kaplan-Meier or Fleming-Harrington method, overall or per group, with 95% confidence limits and the median time per group.
Word and phrase counts in a text field, overall and per group, with stop words, n-grams and the terms most distinctive of each group.
Applies tier tables (commission plans, tax bands, volume discounts) marginally or to the whole amount, per plan, with a breakdown by tier.
Flags spikes and dips per series against a robust rolling median and MAD baseline with weekday effects, centred or trailing.
Counts and sums points within several radii of each site, with exclusive and shared catchment, and the nearest site and distance band per point.
Checks a classifier's predictions against the actual values: a confusion matrix, and precision, recall and F1 score for each class with macro, weighted and micro averages.
Bridges two totals (budget vs actual, year on year) by category as waterfall steps with favourable / adverse labels, per group.
Follows the links of a website from a start page and lists its pages with their title, heading, text and status, the links on each page, and the images.
Multi-criteria scorecards: normalise criteria, apply weights, rank alternatives, apply must-pass thresholds and test how sensitive the winner is to the weights.
Sends a prompt from each record to an Anthropic Claude model and adds the reply as a Response field. Uses your own Anthropic API key.
Sends a prompt from each record to a DeepSeek model and adds the reply as a Response field. Uses your own DeepSeek API key.
Sends a prompt from each record to a Google Gemini model and adds the reply as a Response field. Uses your own Gemini API key.
Sends a prompt from each record to a language model on your own server, through an OpenAI-compatible endpoint, and adds the reply as a Response field.
Reads every record of an Airtable table, or of one of its views, through the Airtable REST API, one record per row.

blocks.displayName: Azure Data Lake Storage Gen2 Blob
blocks.description: Reads one CSV or Parquet file (blob) from a container in an Azure storage account, including Data Lake Storage Gen2, using the account's connection string.
Runs a SQL query (GoogleSQL) on Google BigQuery and outputs the result, with BigQuery's types mapped to Omniscope field types.
Reads a whole Google BigQuery table or view, page by page, with BigQuery's types mapped to Omniscope field types.
Loads the result of a saved Dune query, public or your own: its latest stored result, or a fresh execution. Every page of rows is read, with numbers and dates typed from Dune's column types.
Loads the native-coin balances, or the full transaction lists, of the Ethereum addresses in a field, from the Etherscan API (Ethereum and other chains by chain ID).

Loads the list of airlines from the FlightStats (Cirium Flex) API, one record per airline with its code (FlightStats, IATA, ICAO), name, phone number and whether it is active. Needs a FlightStats App ID and App key.

Loads the list of airports from the FlightStats (Cirium Flex) API, one record per airport with its codes (FlightStats, IATA, ICAO, FAA), name, city, country, time zone, latitude, longitude and elevation. Needs a FlightStats App ID and App key.

Looks up each flight in the input (carrier, flight number and departure date) in the FlightStats (Cirium Flex) schedules and adds its scheduled airports, local departure and arrival times, aircraft type and codeshares. Needs a FlightStats App ID and App key.

Runs a SQL query on Flipside's blockchain data tables through the Flipside API and writes every page of the result. Flipside has wound down its public query tools, so the API may no longer accept queries.
Loads HubSpot companies, contacts, leads, deals, lists, forms, form submissions and associations into records, following every page, or searches contacts and companies.
Loads the projects in a Jira Cloud site and the issues of a project or a JQL search, one record per issue with its status, people, dates, labels and components.
Sends a prompt from each record to an OpenAI model and adds the reply as a Response field. Uses your own OpenAI API key.

For each street name in a field, finds the OpenStreetMap streets with that name through the Overpass API, optionally inside a bounding box, and writes one record per point along each street with its latitude and longitude.
Loads Salesforce data through OAuth 2.0 and the REST API, with a simple object picker that automatically loads all available fields.
Calls any Slack Web API method, such as conversations.list or chat.postMessage, and turns the answer into records, following every page.
Loads the transactions of a Slim CD payment gateway account (the SearchTransactions2 report), filtered by date range, customer, amount, card or transaction details, one record per transaction.
Loads Trello boards, lists, cards, checklists and checklist items, and searches cards, with labels, members and due dates as fields.

Adds the current weather, or a 5-day forecast in 3-hour steps, from OpenWeatherMap to each location in the input, found by latitude and longitude, city or postcode. Needs a free OpenWeatherMap API key.
Reads a SAS transport file (XPORT version 5, .xpt): one dataset as records, plus a list of the datasets in the file and their fields.
For each record, loads the price history of the ticker in a field from Yahoo Finance: open, high, low, close, volume, dividends and splits per day, week, month or shorter interval, between two dates.
Runs a program on the machine that runs Omniscope, once or once per record, passes the input records through and outputs each command's exit code, output and errors.
Reads the documents of a MongoDB collection, all of them or those matching a JSON query, one record per document.
Runs a SQL query on Snowflake, signing in with a password or a key pair, and outputs the result.
Generates a calendar table: calendar and ISO weeks, fiscal periods for any year start, UK or US public holidays, working-day counts and flags.
Extracts the text of every PDF file in a folder, one record per page, with the file name and page number. Optionally writes a .txt file beside each PDF.
Reads a table from an R data file (.rds, .rda or .RData): a data frame, matrix or vector saved from R. A second output lists the objects in the file.
Appends many .rds files saved from R into one output: every .rds file in a folder, or the files listed in an input field. Files with different fields can be lined up first.
Downloads the files in a folder on an SFTP server to the Omniscope server and lists them, ready for an Append files block to load.
Downloads a file, or every file in a folder, from a SharePoint Online document library to the Omniscope server, ready for an Append files block to load.
Logs in to a website through its HTML login form, as a browser would, and outputs the session cookies and every response header, for later HTTP requests that need the session.
Combines the PDF files listed in the input records, in record order, into one PDF file, with an optional bookmark for each file.
Reads a CSV or other delimited file from a GitHub repository into records, or writes the input records to a file in a repository as a new commit.
Loads the input records into a Google BigQuery table, appending them or replacing the table's contents; the table is created if it doesn't exist.
Posts files to an HTTP endpoint as multipart/form-data, one request per file, and records each response's status and body.
Prints a Report tab to a PDF file for each input record, from the tab's address in a field, saving the files in a folder.
Prints one Report tab once per scenario of a multi-tenant configuration, saving a PDF file per scenario in a folder.
Takes a screenshot of each Report tab in the input and makes a PowerPoint file with one slide per tab.
Takes a screenshot of the Report tab at each input record's URL and posts it to a Slack channel with the record's message and the link; optionally also one PDF of all screenshots.
Posts one message to a Slack channel for each input record, as your Slack app's bot, optionally with a file attached.
Sends the input records as a message to a Telegram chat, group or channel through your bot, as text, a table or JSON.
Saves a screenshot (PNG) of the web page at each input record's URL, at a chosen size, and optionally one PDF with a page per screenshot.
Adds a field numbering the records 1, 2, 3 and so on, in the order they arrive, working through the data in chunks so large inputs never have to fit in memory.
Exact age or service in years, months and days, decimal years, bands, next anniversary and upcoming milestones, with 29 February handled.
Replaces names, emails and other text with generated code words, and shifts numbers and dates by random noise, to make a safer copy of a dataset for demos and testing.
Elapsed business hours between timestamps within opening hours, excluding weekends and holidays, with SLA due times and met / breached status.

Maps the many names a field goes by (aliases) to one canonical name, combines fields that hold the same thing, and converts each to a set type with an optional default, following rules kept as data (typed into the block or in a CSV file), working through the data in chunks so large inputs never have to fit in memory.
When its yes/no option (usually linked to a project parameter) is on, starts a separate run of the listed blocks of a project; when it is off, does nothing.
Removes empty rows and fields, fixes missing values, strips unwanted characters and changes case in one step, with a report of what changed.
Compares two versions of a dataset by key: added, removed and changed records, field-level differences with tolerances, and schema differences.
Finds duplicate records, missing values and numeric outliers, and outputs an issue log, the data annotated with its issues, and a copy with missing values filled.
Validates data against a rules table or typed rules (not empty, unique, ranges, lists, patterns, emails, postcodes, field comparisons) with violations per row and per rule.
Expands each start / end date range into one row per day, week, month, quarter or year, with days in each period and amounts prorated by days.
Finds duplicates within a dataset on several match keys, keeps a survivor per group by rules and fills its gaps from the duplicates.
Adds year, quarter, month, week, day and day-name fields for each chosen date field, for filtering and grouping by part of a date without formulas.
Renames the fields of a data set from a list of rules (current name, new name) held in another data set, and lists the rules that matched nothing and the fields left unchanged.
Runs another Omniscope project once per input record, setting its project parameters from the record before each run, and lists the result of every run.

Runs another Omniscope project once per input record in up to three stages, each a separate run of its own blocks, with an optional stage before the loop; sets the project's parameters from each record first.
Sets project parameters in one or more Omniscope projects: each input record gives a project's address and the values for parameters named like its fields.
Finds a centre point (latitude and longitude) for each shape, from records with GeoJSON or WKT shapes or from a GeoJSON file or shapefile, and outputs it with the shape's ID or other fields.
Converts Maidenhead grid square locators (such as IO91wm) to the longitude and latitude of the square's centre.

Finds which region each latitude / longitude point falls in, and adds the region's label to the point's record. The regions come from records with GeoJSON or WKT shapes on a second input, or from a shapefile or GeoJSON file.
Validates, standardises and extracts UK postcodes and splits them into area, district and sector with area name and country, offline.
Fills missing values with the mean, median, mode, a constant, previous / next value or interpolation, optionally within groups, with indicator fields and a summary.
Runs a Kedro project's pipeline on the block's inputs: each input is saved to a named dataset of the project's catalog, and up to two datasets the pipeline produces become the block's outputs.
Turns a text field holding a JSON object into one new field per key, next to the input fields; nested objects and arrays become JSON text.

Turns JSON text into a flat table: each object becomes a record and each array item a record of its own, nested objects become fields such as customer.name, and the input fields are repeated on every record.
Joins each row to the record in force at its date (latest on or before, next, or nearest) per key, with a maximum gap and validity end dates.

Joins two inputs on text fields that are written differently but share words, such as company names or product descriptions. Each record is paired with the record on the other side that shares the most distinctive words.
Finds near-duplicate records within one input (with group IDs), or the best matching record in a second input, using fuzzy text similarity.

Joins the first and second inputs where a number or date field of the first is less than, greater than or equal to a field of the second (<, <=, >, >=, ==), optionally only where another field is equal as well. Every matching pair is output.
Joins each record of the first input to the intervals in the second input that contain its value (a number or a date between a start and an end), optionally only where another field matches as well.
Converts Markdown text in a field (bold, lists, links, headings, tables) to HTML in a new field, keeping the other fields.
Applies one operation (round, scale, share of row or column total, index to base, z-score, fill, text case...) to many fields chosen by list, name pattern or type, with optional row statistics.
Window calculations across rows within groups: previous / next value, change, % change, running total, rolling mean / sum / min / max over rows or days, rank and share of group.
Splits full names into title, first, middle, last and suffix, tidies capitalisation, flags organisations and builds salutations.
Flags low and high outliers in many numeric fields at once, within groups, by IQR, z-score or robust MAD, with bounds and optional capping.
Numbers records in consecutive groups of a chosen size (1 for the first 1,000 records, 2 for the next 1,000 and so on) in a new Partition field, for processing or sending data in batches.
Keeps the chosen fixed fields and turns every other field into records: one record per input record and field, with the field's name and its value. Values of different types become text.
Applies a regular expression to a text field: parse capture groups into fields, replace with back-references, tokenise matches into columns or rows, or flag matches.
Trailing time-window aggregates per key (count, sum, mean, min, max, distinct) for several windows, such as transactions per card in the last 24 hours.
Finds missing, duplicate and out-of-order numbers in invoice, cheque or ticket sequences, per series, with a completeness summary.
Groups each user's timestamped events into sessions by an inactivity gap, adding session IDs to events and producing a session summary with duration, landing and exit events.
Sets project parameters, often of the project it is in, from records holding a parameter name and a value; all values are set in one request.
Parses text fields holding dates in mixed formats (ISO, day-first or month-first, named months, compact, with time zones) into Date fields, and flags the values it could not read.

Cleans up an export with untidy field names: makes the names lower case with underscores, merges fields whose names differ only in case, spaces or dashes, and gives each text field a number, date, yes/no or text type, working through the data in chunks so large inputs never have to fit in memory.
Reorders the fields of the data by name (case-insensitive, with numbers in names in numeric order: Q2 before Q10) or by type, optionally keeping chosen fields first.
Splits a street address such as "Kerkstraat 12A" or "221B Baker Street" into the street name, the house number and a suffix (the letter or addition after the number).
Rescales the chosen number fields to the range 0 to 1 (min-max scaling): each field's lowest value becomes 0, its highest 1, and the rest fall proportionally between.
Draws a reproducible random sample within strata: proportional with a minimum per stratum, equal, fixed number or percentage, with sampling weights and an allocation table.
Renames the fields of the input from rename rules (current name, new name) written in the block or kept in a CSV file, working through the data in chunks so large inputs never have to fit in memory.
Aggregates by a hierarchy of fields with subtotal rows at every level and a grand total, shares of parent and total, in report order.
Assigns records to tiles of a numeric field: quantiles, equal-sum Pareto bands, equal width, standard-deviation bands or manual cut points, optionally within groups.
Turns times of day and durations into a number of milliseconds, seconds, minutes or hours, in a new field for each chosen field, ready to add up, average or compare.
Inserts missing days, weeks, months or other periods in each time series and fills values with zero, the previous value or interpolation, with a gap report.
Keeps the top N items per group by value and rolls the rest into an Other row, with ranks, shares and cumulative shares.
Percent-encodes the text in a field (UTF-8) into a new field, so it can go into a link, a query string or a web request.
Turns HTML character references such as &, é and £ in a text field back into the characters they stand for, in a new field.
Splits text fields that hold several values in one cell, such as one item per line, into one record per value, repeating the other fields.
Counts working days between dates and adds working days to dates, skipping weekends and UK or US public holidays, with SLA checks.
